newsitem.title: USA: Somnus gets FDA marketing ok for snoring treatment.
newsitem.headline: Somnus gets FDA marketing ok for snoring treatment.

text.p: Somnus Medical Technologies Inc said Tuesday it has received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to market its somnoplasty system for treating habitual snoring.

The company said somnoplasty is designed to provide the 40 million Americans who suffer from habitual snoring with a minimally invasive, cost-effective, outpatient therapy that can be performed under local anesthesia.
The company said patients who undergo somnoplasty spend about 30 minutes in the doctor's office and typically return to their normal activities on the same day.
In April 1997, Somnus submitted an application for clearance to the FDA based on a set of patients from six U.S. clinical sites.
The company said results from the trials indicate somnoplasty is safe and comparable in efficacy to other surgical treatments of habitual snoring.
Somnoplasty treats habitual snoring by reducing and tightening tissue in the soft palate and causing the uvula to retract.
The company said the procedure, including patient preparation and administration of local anesthesia, usually takes less than 30 minutes.
Under an agreement between Somnus and Medtronic Inc, Medtronic distributes the somnoplasty system in Europe and selected Pacific Rim countries.
